---

---
title: Your First Game
level: Getting Started
time: 15 min
starter: empty
description: A sprite, an object, a room, and a player you move with the arrow keys.
---
# Your first game

In this tutorial you'll make a player you can move around the screen with the arrow keys.

Each step tells you what to do, then **✔ Check my work** checks it. When it passes, **Next** opens the next step.

Type the code yourself — that's how you learn it.

---

## A sprite

A **sprite** is a picture. Press the **+** beside **Sprites** and pick the **player**.

highlight: add-sprites

```check
sprite player exists
```

---

## An object

An **object** is a thing in your game: it has a sprite, and code that says what it does.

Press the **+** beside **Objects**, type the name **Player**, and press Enter.

highlight: add-objects

```check
object Player exists
```

---

## Give it its sprite

With **Player** open, choose **player** in its **Sprite** box.

highlight: object-sprite

```check
Player has sprite
```

---

## Put it in the room

A **room** is where the game happens. Open **Room1** from the **Rooms** folder, then drag **Player** from the list on the left into the room.

highlight: folder-rooms

```check
room Room1 has at least 1 Player
```

---

## Make it move

Open **Player**, press **Add event** and choose **Step**. A Step event runs every frame — 60 times a second.

Type this into it:

```python
self.x += (keyboard_check("right") - keyboard_check("left")) * 4
self.y += (keyboard_check("down") - keyboard_check("up")) * 4
```

`keyboard_check("right")` is 1 while the right arrow is held, and 0 when it isn't. So right minus left is 1, -1 or 0 — which way to go — and `* 4` is how fast.

highlight: add-event

```check
Player has event step
Player.step uses keyboard_check
after 1 second holding right, Player.x increased
after 1 second holding down, Player.y increased
```

---

## Play it

Press **Play**, click the game, and move with the arrow keys.

highlight: play

```check
game runs 2 seconds without errors
```

---

## You made a game

Your player moves. Ideas to try next:

- Change the `4` to make it faster or slower.
- Add a second sprite and object — a coin, a wall.
- Try the **Collect the Coins** tutorial.

---
title: Collect the Coins
level: Getting Started
time: 20 min
starter: coins-start
description: Touch a coin to collect it, keep score, and show it on screen.
---
# Collect the coins

This game has a maze, coins, and a player who moves with the arrow keys. Press **Play** and try it: the coins don't do anything yet.

You'll make the coins disappear when the player touches them, count them, and show the score.

---

## Touching a coin

Open **Player**, press **Add event**, and under **Collision with** choose **Coin**.

This event runs when the player touches a coin. `other` is the coin it touched. Type:

```python
other.destroy()
```

highlight: add-event

```check
Player has event collision with Coin
Player.collision with Coin uses destroy
after 1 second holding right, instance_number("Coin") < 15
```

---

## Keep score

A **global variable** is one every object can see. Start the score at 0 in Player's **Create** event — add this line under what's there:

```python
global_vars.score = 0
```

Then in the **Collision with Coin** event, under `other.destroy()`:

```python
global_vars.score += 1
```

```check
Player.create uses global_vars
after 1 second holding right, global_vars.score >= 1
```

---

## Show the score

Make a new object called **Hud** (no sprite) and drag it into the room. Give it a **Draw GUI** event — it draws on top of everything:

```python
draw_set_color("white")
draw_text(8, 452, f"Coins: {global_vars.score}")
```

highlight: add-objects

```check
object Hud exists
Hud has event draw gui
Hud.draw gui uses draw_text
room Maze has 1 Hud
game runs 2 seconds without errors
```

---

## A sound

The game already has a **coin** sound. In the **Collision with Coin** event, add:

```python
sound_play("coin")
```

```check
Player.collision with Coin uses sound_play
```

---

## Done

Play it and collect them all. Ideas:

- Show "You got them all!" when `not instance_exists("Coin")`.
- Make some coins worth 5.

---
title: Simple Platformer
level: Platformers
time: 25 min
starter: platformer-start
description: Gravity, solid ground, running and jumping.
---
# A platformer

The level is built from tiles, and some tiles are **solid**. The **Player** is there, but it has no code yet: press **Play**, and nothing moves.

You'll give it gravity, running and jumping.

---

## Speed

Open **Player**, add a **Create** event, and type:

```python
self.vx = 0
self.vy = 0
```

`vx` and `vy` are how fast it moves across and down, in pixels a frame.

```check
Player has event create
Player.create uses vy
```

---

## Running

Add a **Step** event:

```python
move = keyboard_check("right") - keyboard_check("left")
self.vx = move * 4
if move_and_collide(self.vx, 0):
    self.vx = 0
```

`move_and_collide` moves it, but stops it against anything solid — and says whether it hit something.

highlight: add-event

```check
Player.step uses move_and_collide
after 1 second holding right, Player.x increased
```

---

## Gravity

Under that, in the same Step event:

```python
self.vy = min(self.vy + 0.6, 12)
if move_and_collide(0, self.vy):
    self.vy = 0
```

Each frame it falls a little faster, up to 12. Hitting the ground stops the fall.

```check
Player.step uses min
game runs 2 seconds without errors
```

---

## Jumping

Only jump when standing on something. Add, above the gravity lines:

```python
on_ground = not place_free(self.x, self.y + 1)
if on_ground and keyboard_check_pressed("space"):
    self.vy = -11
```

`place_free` says whether a spot is empty. One pixel below your feet not being free means you're standing.

```check
Player.step uses place_free
Player.step uses keyboard_check_pressed
game runs 2 seconds without errors
```

---

## Coins

Add a **Collision with Coin** event to Player:

```python
other.destroy()
sound_play("coin")
```

```check
Player has event collision with Coin
Player.collision with Coin uses destroy
```

---

## Done

You have a platformer. Ideas:

- Face the way you're going: `self.image_xscale = move` when `move != 0`.
- Make the jump higher or the gravity stronger.
- Add an Enemy that you can jump on.

---
title: Blocks to Python
level: Getting Started
time: 15 min
starter: player-start
description: Build an event from blocks, read the Python they make, then turn it into Python.
---
# Blocks to Python

Blocks and Python are the same code, written two ways. You'll build an event from blocks, see the Python it makes, then turn it into Python and carry on typing.

---

## A Step event in blocks

Open **Player**, press **Add event** and choose **Step**. Then press the **Blocks** tab above the code.

highlight: tab-blocks

```check
Player has event step
Player.step is written in blocks
```

---

## Move right

Build this from the blocks on the left:

- from **Logic**, an **if** block
- from **Input**, a **keyboard_check** block in the if's slot — choose **right**
- from **Motion**, **change x by 4** inside the if

highlight: blocks-workspace

```check
Player.step uses keyboard_check
after 1 second holding right, Player.x increased
```

---

## The Python it makes

Look beside the blocks: that's the Python your blocks make. The game only ever runs that Python.

```python
if keyboard_check("right"):
    self.x += 4
```

highlight: blocks-python

---

## Turn it into Python

Press the **Python** tab and say OK. From now on this event is Python.

```check
Player.step is written in python
Player.step uses keyboard_check
```

---

## Now type the rest

Add moving left, in Python, under what's there:

```python
if keyboard_check("left"):
    self.x -= 4
```

```check
after 1 second holding left, Player.x decreased
game runs 2 seconds without errors
```

---

## Done

You've moved from blocks to Python. Anything blocks can do, Python can — and much more.
